Figure 1.Overview of CaSKG. Multiple skill-level signals induce a directed candidate set. A budgeted subset is examined with direction-conditioned removal, substitution, and reordering probes. The resulting evidence assigns edge states and publication weights, producing the published skill graph. Task-conditioned retrieval then propagates query relevance over this graph to return a compact skill context.A four-stage CaSKG pipeline. Candidate relations are induced
from skill-level signals, selected edges are evaluated with removal,
substitution, and reordering probes, edge states determine graph publication,
and personalized PageRank retrieves task-relevant skills from the published graph.
